results.title: Allocated Node Pools for LKS - Latitude.sh
highlights:
Allocated Node Pools for LKS - Latitude.sh

# Allocated Node Pools for LKS

October 19, 2026

Run LKS on Servers you already have. Pick servers from your project and LKS turns them into Kubernetes Nodes, with no new servers to provision.

Put your existing hardware to work

- Use what you already have — Reserved and contracted Servers, including GPUs, run as Kubernetes Nodes.
- Fully managed — LKS handles node setup, repairs and Kubernetes upgrades, just like on-demand Node Pools.
- Mix and match — Run your existing Servers and add on-demand Node Pools for extra capacity, in the same Cluster.
- Your Servers stay yours — When a Server leaves the pool, it returns to your project with a clean OS, on the same contract and billing.

Servers must be BGP-ready and meet a few other requirements. They’re reinstalled when added to a Pool, so back up anything you need first.

# Fixes & Improvements

November 4, 2026

Virtual Machines

- Improved provisioning reliability with safer deployments, more resilient image downloads, better disk handling, and automatic clock synchronisation.

**Identity & Security **

Storage

Metal

- Improved Broadcom and Intel X710 network adapter support across all supported operating systems.
- Reduced provisioning failures across supported hardware platforms.

results.title: File Storage is now available - Latitude.sh
highlights:
# File Storage is now available

October 28, 2026

One filesystem. Multiple servers.

Share files across bare metal servers with persistent NFS storage, at $0.08/GB/month.

- Shared access: Mount the same filesystem on multiple servers.
- Persistent data: Keep your files when servers are reinstalled or removed.
- Flexible capacity: From 32 GB to 100 TB.
- Free traffic: Access your files over a private storage network with no traffic charges.

Available in: 🇺🇸 Ashburn · 🇺🇸 Los Angeles · 🇺🇸 Chicago · 🇺🇸 New York · 🇬🇧 London · 🇯🇵 Tokyo
